name: Mike's Sunday Ride

start_location.address: Desert Breeze Blvd, between McClintock and Rural Rds and Chandler Blvd and Ray Rd, Chandler, AZ

Named for longtime club member Michael Kirk.

name: Whatever You Feel Like Ride

description: A Thursday night ride on whatever bike you have: fixies, mountain bikes, e-bikes, gravel, road, trikes. It covers 10–18 miles after dark from Rio Vista in Peoria and stops as needed for water. Nobody gets left behind.

name: True Beginner Ride
schedule: Every Wednesday evening. The start moves between 6:30 and 7:30 pm with the season (7:00 pm on Sept 30 and Oct 7, 2026). Called off above 105°F, in strong wind or lightning.
pace: Set by the riders' comfort level, on neighborhood streets
founded_note: The group says it has run rides for all skill levels since 2012.
visitor_notes: RSVP on Meetup. Helmets required. Bring front and rear lights, a spare tube, tools and water.
description: A weekly ride for people who are just starting out or getting back on the bike. The group rides neighborhood streets at whatever distance suits the riders, and newcomers learn group-riding basics and etiquette. The group's rule: nobody gets left behind.
evidence: The group's Meetup feed lists the ride on Wed Sept 30 and Wed Oct 7, 2026; the Meetup series runs weekly to Dec 23, 2026 (fetched Sept 30, 2026).

refresh.notes: Heat cancellations are posted on the Meetup event.

name: Bullshifters Saturday Club Ride
schedule: Every Saturday, about half an hour after sunrise. October 2026: 7:00 am on Oct 3 and 10, 7:30 am on Oct 17, 24 and 31. Routes are posted a month at a time.

start_location.name: Moon Valley Park
start_location.address: 7th Ave and Coral Gables, Phoenix, AZ

pace: Faster group averages 19–20 mph, moderate group 15–17 mph
founded_note: Started in 1986 as an employee club of Honeywell Bull.
visitor_notes: Helmets required. The club asks riders to take out a paid membership after an introductory ride.

name: Ahwatukee Climbing Circuit Ride

start_location.name: Philly's Sports Grill, east end of the shopping center at 48th St and Warner

name: Granada Sunday Breakfast Ride

pace: Two groups: the 3s average 15–16 mph, the 4s average 11–13 mph
visitor_notes: The club says visitors are always welcome. Helmets required; bring water.
description: The club's Granada chapter meets every Sunday at Granada Park in central Phoenix and rides in two groups, one around 15–16 mph and one around 11–13 mph. Each week ends at a different breakfast place, named on the club calendar.

name: Night Rider Series @ Trail 100
schedule: Every Wednesday, 6:30 pm, on Trail 100. The meet spot can change with the season or the trailhead; check the Meetup event.
visitor_notes: RSVP on Meetup (capped at 20 riders). Bring lights that last two hours.
description: A weeknight mountain bike ride on Trail 100 in the Phoenix Mountains Preserve: mostly out-and-back with side trails mixed in, 8–10 miles in about two hours. The same group rides South Mountain on Tuesday nights (Taco Tuesday).

name: Saturday Cycling
schedule: Every Saturday. The start moves with the season: 8:30 am Jan, 8:00 Feb, 7:30 Mar, 7:00 Apr, 6:30 May–Aug, 7:00 Sept, 7:30 Oct, 8:00 Nov, 8:30 Dec.

start_location.name: Kiwanis Park, the parking lot on S. All America Way nearest Mill Ave
start_location.address: Kiwanis Park, SE of Mill Ave and Baseline Rd, Tempe, AZ

pace: Standard route is no-drop with a sweep rider; faster riders go around 20 mph
visitor_notes: The club says visitors are always welcome. Helmet required, no earphones.

name: GABA El Tour de Tucson Training Rides
schedule: Sundays through the 11 weeks before El Tour de Tucson (week 6 is Oct 4, 2026). Meet 6:45 am, roll shortly after. Distance grows about 10% a week (66 miles in week 6).

start_location.name: Safeway at Golf Links and Wilmot
start_location.address: Golf Links Rd and Wilmot Rd, Tucson, AZ

pace: Two groups: B (16–18 mph) and C to C+ (12–16 mph), on GABA's scale
visitor_notes: Register through the gatherist.org link on each Meetup event. Know the route (RideWithGPS link on the event), carry flat repair and at least two hours of water.
description: GABA's 11-week build for El Tour de Tucson in November. Two ride leaders run a faster B group and a moderate C/C+ group, with occasional regroups, and the route gets about 10% longer each week. Good for anyone in town training for El Tour.
evidence: GABA's Meetup feed lists 'ETT Training Week #6' for Sun Oct 4, 2026, 6:45 am at the Safeway on Golf Links and Wilmot (fetched Sept 30, 2026).

refresh.notes: Seasonal: the series starts in late summer and ends before El Tour in November.

schedule: Every Tuesday morning, at the same time as the Saturday Shootout A group: 6:30 am from the first Saturday of September, 7:00 am from the second Saturday of October (Oct 10, 2026), 7:30 am from the second Saturday of November, 7:00 am from March, 6:30 am from early April, 6:00 am from the third Saturday of April.

start_location.name: Near University Blvd and Euclid Ave, by the University of Arizona
start_location.address: University Blvd and Euclid Ave, Tucson, AZ

pace: Fast; natural group splits as the pace rises

host.name: Tuesday Morning Fast Ride (documented by Fair Wheel Bikes)

refresh.notes: Start time follows the Shootout's seasonal table on the same page.

name: World Famous Swami's Saturday Ride
schedule: Every Saturday: A group rolls 8:15 am, B group 8:19 am. On the first Saturday of the month the route runs in reverse. Some Saturdays add a special training ride from the same start.
pace: Two groups, A and B, leaving four minutes apart
visitor_notes: The club's weekly-rides page lists its rides as open to non-members.
description: North County San Diego's best-known Saturday ride. A and B groups leave Cadence Cyclery on Coast Highway 101 four minutes apart and usually ride the classic Elfin Forest / Del Dios loop, about 37 miles. On the first Saturday of the month the loop runs in reverse.

name: Praline Croissant Women's/NB Ride
schedule: Fridays at 6:30 am in season (listed Sept 11, Sept 18, Oct 2 and Oct 9, 2026). Leaves on time. Rain calls go up by 10 pm the night before and again at 5:30 am.

name: Saturday Tualatin Ride
visitor_notes: Non-members sign up on the ride's page. Road bikes only, no TT or tri bikes. Load the route on a bike computer in case you come off the back.
description: A fast, hilly Saturday ride of about 62 miles from Tualatin Community Park, southwest of Portland. It starts as one group and may split into speed groups, with a food stop about halfway; riders need to be comfortable in a paceline at 20 mph. Free parking at the park.
evidence: The club's ride calendar lists the ride every Saturday in September 2026, and its Oct 3, 2026 listing gives 9:00 am from Tualatin Community Park (fetched Sept 30, 2026).
